questions.stem: What is the difference between evaporation and boiling?

options.text: Evaporation only happens to water, while boiling can happen to any liquid
Evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature, while boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point
Evaporation absorbs energy while boiling releases energy
There is no difference; they are the same process

questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid at any temperature and is a slow process. Boiling occurs throughout the liquid but only at the boiling point, is a fast process, and produces bubbles. Both involve the change from liquid to gas, but they differ in where and when they occur.
